title: Opening-material vault (controlled)
description: Custody record for commitment opening material. SUPERSEDES the earlier 'salt registry' guidance, which was wrong: centralizing all unrevealed salts in an ordinary registry creates a high-value disclosure point, and opening salts preserve hiding only while secret.

SUPERSEDES.guidance: 'Maintain a salt registry so verification step 11 is answerable.'
SUPERSEDES.defect: Implied a broadly accessible list of unrevealed salts. Disclosure of that list would destroy hiding for every open commitment simultaneously - a single point of total failure for the mechanism it was meant to support.
SUPERSEDES.correction: Uniqueness is checked INSIDE the protected vault at creation. Unrevealed salts are never exposed for global duplicate checking. Disclosed salts move to a historical opening register only AFTER reveal.

dual_property_requirement.confidentiality_before_reveal: Disclosure destroys hiding and voids the blind-inject design.
dual_property_requirement.availability_at_reveal: Loss makes the commitment permanently unopenable - indistinguishable from refusing to reveal.
dual_property_requirement.rule: Backup must protect BOTH. Solving only one breaks the commitment process in a different direction.

opening_salt.description: SECRET. Never leaves the vault before reveal.

package_digest.description: Internal verification digest, for vault-side integrity checking.

created_at.description: TRUSTED time, not self-declared - see trust model sec 20.5a.

recovery_test.description: Evidence id of the most recent successful recovery test.

operating_rules: Check salt uniqueness INSIDE the protected vault at creation.
Publish disclosed salts into a historical opening register AFTER reveal.
Do NOT expose unrevealed salts merely to support global duplicate checking.

Treat reuse detection primarily as CSPRNG-HEALTH EVIDENCE. With correctly generated 256-bit or larger salts, accidental collision is extraordinarily unlikely; a collision indicates a broken generator, not an ordinary duplicate.
Encrypt backups under keys DISTINCT from the authorization, execution, evidence, and assessment keys.
Require dual control or threshold recovery for backup access.
Test recovery BEFORE the exercise, without prematurely exposing the actual opening material (recover to a sealed check, not to a readable copy).
Record backup loss or failed recovery as a READINESS REGRESSION.
Destroy opening secrets only after the retention policy permits, while PRESERVING the revealed package and the verification evidence.

verification_step_11_resolution.question: How is 'the opening_salt has not appeared in another commitment' answered without a global plaintext list?
verification_step_11_resolution.answer: The vault answers it at CREATION time, inside the protected boundary, before the salt is ever used. White does not need the list; White needs an attestation from the vault that the uniqueness check ran. After reveal, the salt is in the historical opening register and is checkable openly.
verification_step_11_resolution.attestation_field: Record the uniqueness-check result as evidence at commitment time; expose the result, never the corpus.

regression_triggers: vault encryption key shared with any of the five program keys
